items.title: Johnny DeDroit Interview, 1969-12-04
items.q: Mr. Garinger who was the general manager and a personal friend of mine

ctx.x: Alright, what about The Strand? I'll bring back an incident. The Strand...

The Strand was a long picture theater. And it had... Most of the time it had Don Filippini as the director. He could get more out of a waltz and most of them could get out of a symphony. Then afterwards it had Castro Carraza who went over to the singer. But he couldn't play Stardust unless he got the record and found out what the tempo was. He didn't know A from a bull's foot but he could stand up there and direct the orchestra. He was stiff as a post. Mr. Barr used to tell him, Castro get down off that sump box.…
I said, we all that shit.

items.title: Johnny DeDroit Interview, 1973-03-16
items.q: Mr. Garinger, who was the general manager... He said, Johnny, you have a fine orchestra... He gave me a contract for two years.

ctx.x: We were supreme for, I'll say, the other bands that made maybe perhaps a greater reputation, because they left town. But we stayed in New Orleans and made a living. And even sent the recording outfit to New Orleans to record my orchestra and other local orchestras. And the recordings were not good because they didn't demand that they sent. He was more intent on having a good time than he was making good records. But the records I made in New York in the studio, well, they were made properly. Well, naturally all…
What was the question? I'm lost.
